thread:
nate: Quick follow-up from the fused-attn RFC: we need to decide the runtime routing for fused QKV + bias+rope variant when dropout is disabled at inference. Thoughts?
marco: Short answer: prefer fused path when sequence_len >= 64 and batch_size >= 4. keeps KV cache layout consistent.
ada: @marco do we have perf curves? I remember a corner where fused QKV blew up memory for very long sequences.
marco: perf curves on my laptop are noisy but the cluster runs show stable 1.8-2.4x token/s vs unpacked for typical seq lengths. the memory issue was for seq>2048 on 16k model with unsharded KV.
ada: got it. question: how do we detect "dropout disabled"? many customers still ship models with dropout=0 but training flags vary.
ate: runtime should treat model config dropout==0 OR serving_inference_mode flag as indicator. both are present in model manifest.
ada: +1. Also we need deterministic outputs for evals — fused reorder sometimes changed fp32 rounding.
sophia: We should have a gold eval set with quantile diffs + exact-match spot checks for safety. If fused path deviates beyond 1e-6 relative or changes top-1 tokens in more than 0.05% cases -> block rollout.
yara: Also consider bias+rope fusion interacting with rotary offset aliasing. I've seen token misalignment when rope applied before bias add in a fused kernel. need clear contract: fusion applies bias THEN rotary.
marco: Agreed. kernel contract: inputs are Q,K,V (maybe packed QKV), bias vectors (per-head), and rotary params (cos,sin,offset). kernel applies bias add, then rope, then matmul. we'll add a mode flag for alternate ordering for legacy models.
sophia: For rollout: canary route to 5% traffic for 24h with eval hooks + error budget. If latency regresses >5% or model-quality alert fires -> auto-rollback.
ate: What about KV caching layout? fused packed QKV expects contiguous packed heads; our runtime accepts both packed and separate layouts. We need a low-overhead conversion path for old checkpoints.
ada: conversion should be lazy during first forward with an async background copy to GPU memory. avoid sync copies on hot paths.
yara: test plan: unit tests for ordering + small random seeds, end-to-end eval harness for 10 public prompts, perf microbenchmarks across seq len [8,32,64,256,1024], and memory check for seq up to 4096.
marco: CI tasks: add fused-kernel smoke to nightly, add deterministic kernel artifacts to release candidate artifacts. eng-ci-bot: queued job #4592: run fused-attn-smoke on p4d-xlarge nightly.
ate: API/manifest change: add model_manifest.fusion_support = ["qkv_packed","bias_rope_fused","dropoutless_infer"] and runtime will consult route policy to decide. keep defaults conservative (disabled) and opt-in per-model.
sophia: Can we allow automatic opt-in after passing a validation suite? customers prefer seamless but safe opt-in is fine.
yara: add opt-in TTL and revert hook so customer can opt-in but we auto-revert if their latency or accuracy changes.
marco: Implementation notes: kernel selector heuristics -> cost_model(seq_len,batch,model_dim,kv_sharding,device_mem); if fused beneficial and contract-compatible -> route to fused kernel; else fallback. Export telemetry: chosen_kernel, seq_len, batch, latency, token_cost.
ada: One more: expose a debug flag to force_fused=true/false per request for A/B testing.
ate: Sounds good. I'll draft a short follow-up RFC with rollout checklist and tests. who wants to review?
marco: I'll take the perf and kernel contract sections.
sophia: I'll own the eval + rollback criteria.
yara: I'll add KV cache conversion and runtime selector tests.
ada: I'll add deterministic checks and manifest schema updates.
eng-ci-bot: job #4592 started, ETA ~18m. logs: https://ci.redwood.internal/jobs/4592
marco: cool. Nate — can you add the model_manifest snippet in the RFC? then we can merge and schedule canary next week.
nate: will do, thanks everyone :thumbsup:
